_what: Act V's record: the words that go on screen, the windows they occupy, and the build parameters that produce the delivered master. It exists so act V's inputs are COMMITTED rather than living only in ~/Videos/wolves-natali (#152): an act cut entirely outside the repo gives the Nat half of the dictated Kat/Nat round (#118) nowhere to land, and no check can tell whether a revision took. scripts/build_natali.py reads this; editing a line here changes the film. Same shape as stories/04-kat-plates.json.
_provenance: The copy is reproduced from ~/Videos/wolves-natali/render/render-plates.mjs and the windows from render/run-natali.sh, both of which built the delivered file. This is a RECORD of what shipped, not a new edit. Nothing here is invented.
title: Natali
_source: Owner-supplied source. The act is lifted out of the middle of it: 357.45 is the first content frame after the portal-transit black, a clean cut out of black into the Pale Heart arrival, and 382.70 is where the cinematic's own fade to black completes (blackdetect's first fully-black frame is 382.54, so the cut holds ~0.15 s of black). Footage is never committed.

trim._note: Clip time = source - 357.45; every window below is clip time. Input seek is frame-accurate here because the cut is re-encoded: ffmpeg decodes from the preceding keyframe and discards to 357.45, and setpts/asetpts pin the timeline to 0. Native 59.94 fps is preserved -- no fps filter. UNLIKE ACT IV, the picture carries a final fade: the cinematic resolves into its own fade to black and the cut lands with it.

letterbox._note: 2.40:1, measured: cropdetect at limit=44 gives crop=1920:800:0:140. The limit matters -- these matte bars are dark grey (Y~30) rather than true black, so a low-limit cropdetect misreads them as content. Dialogue plates seat INSIDE the bottom matte and never cover picture.

reveal._note: Natali's Guardian card, held over the walk. It sits just above the matte line in the lower third (reveal.html bottom:336px, bottom-left) rather than inside the matte where the pills go.
reveal._not_repo_rendered: The nameplate card is NOT rendered from this record. It was screenshotted from ~/Videos/wolves-natali/render/reveal.html, and its copy is Natali's authored Guardian identity, reproduced verbatim from the website's characters.json and never written here. build_natali.py consumes the existing PNG from the project folder. Same rule, and same reason, as act IV's.

bed._note: OWNER PICK, 2026-08-11: the Shudder bed with NO SFX layer is the shipped cut -- 'this one is awesome'. 20 bars at 189.98 BPM, ending on the song's real final chord decaying across the reveal fade. Two later experiments were rejected by ear and are not defaults: a hybrid-SFX mix (v2) and a louder demucs-based v3. A second bed, Nightwish's 'Wish I Had an Angel (Instrumental, Remastered)' (xgL1oBwVG6M), was built for the v2 pass and survives at render/music-natali-wisha.wav; its ending is a deliberate compromise, faded over its last bar because an intro section has no final chord to land on the reveal. The Shudder bed does resolve, which is why it won.
bed._verification: Instrumental VERIFIED on the exact bed window rather than trusted from the title -- demucs stem analysis plus a whisper pass over the isolated, amplified vocal stem. Recorded in full in ~/Videos/wolves-natali/STORYBOARD.md.
bed._usage_class: third_party_copyrighted -- see the rights section of AGENTS.md. Not committed here; staged in ~/Videos/wolves-natali/sources/.

delivered._note: THIS is what ~/Videos/Wolves/Prod/05-nat.mp4 hardlinks: FLAC stereo, measured 1804652 bit/s. run-natali.sh's own DEFAULTS build the OTHER file (AAC 5.1), exactly as act IV's script does.

variant_51._note: The 5.1 sibling, NOT delivered. The artist's stereo mix passes through bit-exact as FL/FR and the only added channel is an additively-derived LFE; FC/BL/BR are digital silence. ffmpeg's `surround` filter is deliberately not used -- it resynthesises the soundfield and adds ~43 ms of latency.

variant_sfx._note: The REJECTED hybrid: gated source transients mixed under the bed, built on the owner's instruction ('Re-attempt it: mix the source game SFX under the music') and then rejected by ear in favour of the bed-only cut. Kept because a rejected experiment is provenance, not clutter -- without it the next person re-runs it.

encode._loop_framerate_note: run-natali.sh passed NO `-framerate` on its still inputs, unlike run-kat.sh which passed 60. The delivered master was built that way, so this act records the absence rather than inheriting act IV's value.

_plate_kind: Every dialogue plate is `kind: chat` -- tools/plate.py's port of the wolves plate.html pill, which is this repo's renderer for it. The delivered master's plates were screenshotted from plate.html itself; a rebuild from this manifest re-renders them with plate.py instead. On act IV the two agreed to 1px of width and 2px of height with the top-left corner exact, so a rebuild is compared rather than assumed identical.
_timing: `at` + `dur` are tools/plate.py's own manifest fields, so this file renders with `plate.py render --manifest` unmodified. `fade_out_at` is absolute clip time, matching the ffmpeg `fade=t=out:st=` it generates.
unresolved: `Krook` and `Ihor` are not bound in vocab/casting.yaml. They are reproduced as the delivered film spells them, capitalised as the render script had them, and binding them is #26's territory.
Avatars are NOT committed (they are people's photographs). The builder resolves them against the project folder and plate.py degrades to the drawn crest for any it cannot read.

Nick (the docs.bazzite.gg voice) has no avatar in render/ and no binding in vocab/casting.yaml: his three pills render with the drawn crest until render/nick.jpg exists. The speaker labels 'Nat'/'Nick'/'Kat' are the owner's own from #118, reproduced verbatim.
